items.title: Bangladesh U-19s begin Afghanistan series with 33-run win
items.summary: Bangladesh’s new-look U-19 team began their campaign in style, beating Afghanistan by 33 runs in the opening match of a four-match Youth ODI series at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman on Saturday.

items.title: Litton ruled out of tri-series; Miraz misses opener with fever
items.summary: Bangladesh ODI captain Litton Das has been ruled out of the ongoing tri-nation series in the UAE due to a right hip joint issue, a Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) medical official said on Saturday.

items.title: Tigers suffer heavy defeat to Zimbabwe
items.summary: Bangladesh suffered a 99-run defeat to Zimbabwe in the opening match of the UAE ODI Tri-series at the Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi on Saturday.

items.title: Bangladesh’s tri-series record: One title in 13 attempts
items.summary: Bangladesh’s only tri-series title came in Ireland in 2019, when they beat the West Indies by five wickets under the Duckworth-Lewis method in the final.

items.title: Tri-series puts Litton’s leadership in focus
items.summary: Litton Das took over as Bangladesh’s ODI captain at the end of July, but his first test as skipper since replacing Mehidy Hasan Miraz comes almost three months later, with the tri-series involving Zimbabwe and Afghanistan beginning today.

items.title: 'If we play good cricket, why not?': Litton backs Tigers to go all the way in tri-series
items.summary: “If we play good cricket, why not?” Newly appointed ODI captain Litton Das fell back on the age-old wisdom that Bangladesh players so often reach for in press conferences when asked to predict positive outcomes. In this case, the question was whether Bangladesh could go all the way and become champions in the tri-nation series against Zimbabwe and Afghanistan.
